stem: A media company needs consistently fast dashboard queries over very large column subsets and sustained analytical concurrency.

choices.text: Use Amazon Redshift with columnar storage for analytical scan workloads.
Use Athena as the primary always-on warehouse with guaranteed low-latency concurrency targets.
Use a transactional relational instance as the long-term analytics warehouse.
Use a key-value primary table and aggregate with point-lookups for warehouse queries.

rationale: Redshift is designed for columnar analytical scan performance and high-concurrency warehouse use cases. Athena is excellent for many ad hoc patterns but does not match this always-on warehouse latency target framing. Transactional relational instances are not the primary fit for large-scale analytical warehouse concurrency. Key-value point-lookups are mismatched to broad analytic scan and aggregation needs.
